messages.author: 051b8654c3457b56
messages.subject: arrange() is great
parts:
Hi, fun story -- I've been writing code like

z=subset(d,x==5); z[order(z$accuracy),]

for a really long time, and recently I was thinking about writing a
function to streamline the reordering so the temporary variable isn't
necessary.

Today I was looking at plyr 1.0 and found that arrange() does
*exactly* that. Great!

That is all,
Brendan
--
http://anyall.org

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: arrange() is great
parts:
Hi all,

I have one small issue with arrange(), it's also the name I use in the
gridExtra package to layout various grid graphics in one page. Both
packages use namespaces, so the risk of conflict is low, but depending
on the order in which the packages are loaded one might have to use
plyr::arrange() or gridExtra::arrange() which would certainly cause
confusion. I guess the best option is for me to come up with a new
name and re-submit a new version on CRAN. Suggestions? I can only
think of grid.arrange().

Best,

baptiste
